html:
The Anglo-Mysore Wars were four wars between the East India Company and the kingdom of Mysore, fought between 1767 and 1799. Mysore under Hyder Ali and his son Tipu Sultan was the hardest Indian enemy the Company faced.

  • First, 1767 to 1769: Hyder's cavalry rode to the gates of Madras and he dictated the peace.
  • Second, 1780 to 1784: Hyder invaded the Carnatic with 80,000 men and destroyed a British force at Pollilur, the worst British defeat in India to that date. He died in 1782; Tipu fought on, and the peace gave back all conquests.
  • Third, 1790 to 1792: the governor-general Cornwallis, allied with the Marathas and the Nizam of Hyderabad, besieged Tipu's capital. Tipu gave up half his kingdom and two young sons as hostages.
  • Fourth, 1799: Tipu had sought help from France. A British army stormed Srirangapatna on 4 May, and Tipu was killed fighting at the gate.

Mysore's strength was a modern army with French-trained infantry, a strong treasury and iron-cased war rockets (see Mysorean rockets). Its weakness was that its neighbours feared it more than they feared the British.

The old Hindu dynasty was put back as a British dependant. Arthur Wellesley, later Duke of Wellington, learnt his trade here.
